title: The Ale-Chemy Knights
imageAlt: Ale-Chemy Knights symbol: a shield containing a hammer, a potion flask and a foaming ale tankard on a parchment background
imageCaption: The symbol of the Ale-Chemy Knights.
dek: A self-funded adventuring and mutual-aid cooperative whose members lend equipment, organize craftspeople and supplies, welcome newcomers, and support public works and reconstruction.

facts.Motto: One for all… And all for one!

facts.Status: Key members repeatedly absent or missing

body:
Canon ruling: the Ale-Chemy Knights are a distinct faction. Their main members are Tobias, Farkur, and Ryvyt.

The Ale-Chemy Knights began as a small fellowship organized around mutual support, practical work, and a shared call: “One for all…” — “And all for one!” By late 2025 and early 2026 their work included a crafting and logistics cooperative, equipment lending, resource gathering and scouting, public-works sponsorship, property holding, newcomer support, and an increasingly influential merchant network.

The best supported description is a self-funded adventuring cooperative and mutual-aid institution. It is not established as Prima’s government, a standing army, a charity, or a conventional private shop. Its usefulness and its growing soft power are both part of the record.

The history follows a change in scale: welcome and guidance become a worksite, a shop, a supply network and civic infrastructure. Each step creates useful capacity, but also new costs and dependence on particular specialists.

17 November 2024 · Friendly Guides and Grub

The institutional idea predates the named faction. At the Common Man, Farkur pitches “Farkur’s Friendly Guides and Grub,” a Gate-side caravan service offering newcomers maps, food, ale, local curiosities, and eventually paid carriage transport. The proposal is entrepreneurial and comedic as well as helpful; Farkur openly discusses profit and attracting customers.

Pappy warns that the Gate and surrounding land are spiritually significant. The later Knights system grows from this smaller idea, but the continuity does not prove the Ale-Chemy Knights already formally existed in November 2024.

January–early 2025 · Ciderwood gives the idea a base

At Ciderwood Sanctum on Forevermoore, a very small auxiliary island off Eovar’s coast, Farkur expands the Gate-side proposal: welcome arrivals, explain the world, provide maps and transport, connect useful people, record skills, and establish communication and emergency response. Forevermoore remains a minor local holding; the work at its base helps explain the Knights’ development.

Animal space, training, a forge, orchard work and unfinished construction give the idea a physical setting. Proposals for further laboratories and brewing space are not proof that every building was finished. Farkur’s coordination of Green Bean, Fangs and other training efforts reflects the same principle he applies to people: different strengths can accomplish more together.

The base also exposes the cost of permanence. Timber, buildings, transport, training and equipment require time and money; an orchard cannot immediately fund the work. Farkur’s desire for less morally dubious income leads toward the harder question of sustaining an institution.

Early 2025 · Tobias makes the welcome usable

Tobias Goodbarrel demonstrates the system with Fredrick: a safe seat, food, orientation, a map, lodging and employment information, escort toward Pristinia, and personal financial assistance. The welcome has become something another person can perform, rather than a proposal dependent on Farkur being present.

Tobias describes the aim as helping adventurers become independent. Maps, work, contacts and access to equipment are ways to give a newcomer choices. This encounter establishes a working example, not a guarantee that every arrival receives the same support.

May 2025 onward · Ryvyting Creations tests the system

Ryvyting Creations, owned and operated by Ryvyt in Pristinia, brings the Knights’ plans into contact with customers, stock and material shortages. The shop account places soft-opening preparations in May 2025: Ryvyt readies a forge and modest inventory, but an enhanced shield cannot be made because uncommon metals and recipe plants are unavailable.

Ryvyt’s disappointment came from having a recipe and the skill to use it, but lacking materials. Making the forge useful required Ruben’s scouting, component hunters, transport and reliable records.

July 2025 · shared stock, property and bookkeeping

By 25 July, the Knights circulate equipment through a shared inventory. Ryvyt borrows magical items and a Bag of Holding for a job; Farkur records the loans. When Coralyn’s fabrication needs exceed his skill, Farkur directs her to Ryvyt. Specialization works because requests and resources reach the person able to use them.

At the shop, Farkur keeps records and helps with sales, tracking stock, recipes, costs and transactions. Individually owned goods, shared Knights inventory and the building itself require separate accounting. Bookkeeping becomes part of the infrastructure that lets people cooperate without treating every resource as one person’s property.

Farkur credits Pappy with paying for the location and discusses a deed arrangement symbolically framed around ten pieces of jerky. These are attributed property accounts; the established owner and operator of Ryvyting Creations is Ryvyt. Pappy’s material support does not establish sole control of the Knights or a formal membership rank.

Money remains tight and work scarce. Even so, the Knights vote to purchase a tavern in Eovar while Farkur repairs it. The collective decision establishes an organizational project without making all Knights property Farkur’s private estate.

How the supply network works

  1. Find and record: scouts locate materials and preserve routes and resource sites.
  2. Recover and transport: hunters, harvesters, purchasers and carriers bring usable inputs back.
  3. Track and transform: records distinguish stock, costs and ownership; crafters, smiths and builders turn inputs into equipment or structures.
  4. Put to use: the shop and shared pool support sales, exchanges, loans, rentals and projects.
  5. Reinvest: revenue and pooled capital support more materials, paid labor, equipment, transport, property and public work.

This describes the Knights’ operating model, not an audited account of every transaction. Ryvyting Creations is one place where the network becomes visible, rather than the whole institution.

Spell access and Fenwick’s civic connections

Fenwick d’Jorasco advertises the shop’s spell collection as a supplement for wizards unable to find what they need in the public library. Access to especially powerful magic is described more cautiously and with his involvement. Advertising, available spell knowledge and proposed library copying remain different claims; Ryvyt is not established as the creator or personal possessor of every offered spell.

Fenwick is a significant allied institution-builder. His Silver Spire turns personal magical resources into baths, care, shelter and community space in Eovar. The Knights connect a wider network of specialists to crafting, logistics and public projects. Their work can reinforce one another, but the Spire and Vital Chain remain distinct institutions.

Late 2025 · maps, walls, ships, and a mature economy

Scouts and caravans receive regional maps. Farkur and Ruben add symbols, resource sites, field discoveries, older route marks, and preserved return information through tools including a Cartographer’s Map Case and Elder Cartography Glossary. Ruben’s field principle—“Flight now, haul later”—captures the division of labor: one member can find and preserve a resource even when another must extract or transform it.

The Knights apply the same coordination of materials, money and specialists to Pristinia wall upgrades and at least two towers. Paid construction comes with supervision, minimum-work expectations and restrictions on unsafe solo labor. Private organization becomes civic capacity, without granting the Knights governmental authority. By December 8, Ruben describes a mature system that purchases materials, pays specialists, gathers components, crafts and rents equipment, finances eventual acquisition, buys local goods for resale, invests in businesses, maintains pooled money, supports fortifications, and prepares for reconstruction and war logistics.

Ruben describes magical equipment rented at roughly ten percent of cost per mission with ownership after a twelfth mission. Gregory Greenleaf questions the effective financing cost. The two disagree: the Knights call the money necessary to keep projects and supply chains moving; Gregory’s objection prevents that self-description from becoming an objective verdict of fairness.

By December 2025 the organization reports two ships bringing goods from elsewhere and discusses taking its larger troupe through the Convergence toward Gael. Tobias is described as missing again by December 8, leaving the group without a major builder.

February 2026 · the storefront closes as work shifts

The Ryvyting account describes ordinary retail closing as the Knights redirect their main efforts toward Gael and lack enough people to staff the Pristinia shop. Important stock leaves with the group; shelves are largely emptied. Later proposals for caretaking and repairs leave the building’s subsequent use open.

The transition reveals both increased reach and continuing dependence on specific people. It establishes closure and movement of resources; it does not prove that every intended reconstruction project was completed.

14 February 2026 · reputation becomes infrastructure

When Iron Saint Valorum asks Draven Montauk for guidance toward Pristinia, Draven names the Ale-Chemy Knights as the best information source and gives him a special handbell. According to Draven, the bell makes no ordinary audible sound but can be heard by the Knights. Its maker, range, network size, and whether every Knight hears every use remain unknown.

Draven identifies Farkur and Ryvyt as founders and says both are away on an important job. He directs Valorum to the Knights for help even while their founders are absent.

29 March 2026 · a founder submits to judgment

Farkur voluntarily disarms and accepts shackles before the Guardians. He admits repairing the escape ship whose restored rudder enabled the flight connected to Commander Yvette’s murder. He denies knowing about or participating in the killing, but accepts responsibility for enabling the escape and failing to report what he knew. He repeats that account under truth-working.

The Guardians neither imprison nor execute him. Farkur identifies himself and Ryvyt as the Knights’ founders, offers the faction’s bell as a promise of future aid, and visits the graves with Gregory. The scene does not erase culpability; it shows the organization’s public ideals being tested against a founder’s own actions.

April–May 2026 · civic power becomes measurable

By 17 April, Melian reports Pristinia’s finances as stable and calls the Knights’ contributions invaluable. In the same policy debate, Camilla argues that their influx of gold can finance defense, agriculture, and trade. The exchange confirms that Ale-Chemy capital has become part of public planning, while leaving the fairness and durability of that dependence open to scrutiny.

On 15 May, Lady Severina offers the Knights’ Eovar tower as a place for petrified victims and ties restoration of the quarry to completing walls the Knights began. Their holdings, construction, and money are therefore no longer background flavor: each has become infrastructure other communities plan around.

26 May–21 August 2026 · loss and a mixed legacy

Ryvyt arrives aboard an Ale-Chemy ship on 26 May and calls himself the “remaining founder.” The phrase proves that Ryvyt understands the founders’ situation as a loss; it does not by itself establish whether Farkur is dead, missing, absent, or removed from leadership.

On 21 August, Eovar Harbor Master Raven Joyner credits Master Fenwick and the Ale-Chemy Knights with substantial good work. Her assessment is deliberately mixed: adventurers saved people from pirates, later staged a prison break, attract danger, and nevertheless rebuild and improve lives. The Knights’ public role is neither spotless heroism nor simple corruption. It is consequential civic power whose benefits and risks are both visible.

Founders and main members

  • Farkur S. Gemblenagin — founder, organizer, builder and quartermaster; connects capabilities and maintains the records that keep shared work moving.
  • Ryvyt — founder and lead crafter; turns the network’s gathered materials into finished equipment. “King of the Forge” is a playful acknowledgment of his craft, not a formal office.
  • Tobias Goodbarrel — main member, builder and newcomer guide; makes the organization’s services usable by individual people. A shop synthesis reports Farkur calling him a founder, but the confirmed founder roster remains Farkur and Ryvyt pending recovery of that scene.

Operational contributors and allies

  • Ruben — scout, prospector and operational representative. “Flight now, haul later” makes exploration reusable: later workers can follow recorded routes to identified resources. His explanation of the economy shows organizational knowledge extending beyond Farkur.
  • Pappy — important property and financial supporter in Farkur’s account of the Pristinia shop, alongside his wider community role. Funding, ownership and formal membership are separate questions.
  • Anky — inner-circle associate and religious intermediary, often called the Knights’ Saint; exact formal status remains imprecise.
  • Fenwick — civic ally, public promoter and bridge to magical and community infrastructure; his own institutions retain their separate identity.

Severina, Green Bean and Fangs also belong to the wider history. Association does not automatically establish membership. Ryvyt’s Delerium research remains personal research rather than automatic Knights policy.

Gael reconstruction and the open-air market

By 19 September 2026 the Knights had established an open-air market in Gael with areas divided by skill set. Marius remembered the region as having almost no economy; his comparison remains attributed, while the market itself confirms that the Knights’ planned reconstruction produced a durable civic result.

The missing Knights

By that same September record, Farkur and other Knights had vanished. “Vanished” establishes absence, not cause: it does not say whether they were lost, captured, displaced, concealed, or pursuing an unreported mission. Ryvyt reportedly took the disappearance hard. Tobias’s repeated earlier absence makes the institution’s dependence on key specialists an established vulnerability, but Tobias’s status at this later moment remains unclear.

Service, influence and specialist dependence

The Knights describe fellowship, contribution and practical service, with Tobias emphasizing independence. Their strength lies in connecting different specialists; their weakness is that a missing builder, crafter or organizer can still interrupt the whole chain. The retail closure and repeated absences make that vulnerability concrete.

Commerce pays for service, but charging for equipment, holding property and financing public work also concentrate influence. Gregory’s criticism of rental terms and Eovar’s mixed assessment remain part of the history. Neither public benefit nor economic power cancels the other.

Development at a glance

PeriodDevelopmentWhat it changes
17 Nov 2024Friendly Guides and Grub proposalPractical, commercial precursor to newcomer support.
Early 2025Ciderwood work and Tobias’s welcomeA base and a demonstrated service emerge; the founding date remains open.
May–July 2025Ryvyting preparations, shortages and shared stockCrafting needs reliable supply, loans and bookkeeping.
Late 2025Maps, paid public works and reported shipsSpecialized cooperation supports civic projects and wider transport.
Feb 2026Retail closure, Gael shift and Draven’s bellResources move while reputation routes newcomers toward the Knights.
Mar–Aug 2026Confession, civic reliance and reported founder-lossThe network’s obligations, influence and vulnerabilities become visible.
By Sep 2026Gael market and missing KnightsA completed civic result coexists with unresolved disappearances.

Open record

  • When did the fellowship formally adopt its name, rules, and membership structure?
  • Who legally or socially owns the organization’s shared assets and how are profits distributed?
  • What remains of Ryvyting Creations after retail closure, and did it reopen?
  • How extensive is the handbell network and who can hear it?
  • How did the planned Gael reconstruction produce the later market, and which members managed it?
  • Who disappeared with Farkur, what caused the disappearance, and where was Tobias?
  • What did Ryvyt do after learning the others were gone?

What the Knights leave behind

The Knights’ history begins with a modest problem: how to help someone arriving through the Gate without knowledge, food or a route onward. Workshops, scouts, records, equipment and transport grow from the effort to make that help repeatable. Public works and the Gael market show the same system reaching beyond individual adventurers.

Their legacy is the attempt to build capacity that survives the end of a quest. That capacity helps people and creates influence; its durability when key members leave remains one of the history’s central questions.

Aid before trade

During the pirate hostage crisis, Fenwick, Brianna and Ithilrune visit a rebuilding coastal refugee settlement on Gael. Edgar, who is organizing fishing and construction, reports eight captives and three pirate ships; those numbers are his account. Fenwick unloads the Knights’ gifts and helps move residents toward the tower for safety. Brianna entertains the children with conjured snow. Edgar asks for building materials, furniture, cooking equipment, healing kits and livestock, and welcomes a proposed Knights outpost. The settlement has about two hundred people by his estimate and no chosen name. The branch establishes delivered aid and a prospective relationship, not a completed outpost, a hostage rescue or an identification with later refugee groups.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

What adventurer wealth owes the town

Katherine points out that five or ten thousand gold is beyond ordinary villagers’ means while adventurers spend it quickly. Farkur responds by describing the Ale-Chemy Knights’ plans to rebuild, improve trade and defense, and give back to the community that welcomed them. His earlier notice offers a temporary waiver of the building fee and discounted materials, with the town’s land fee still due. These are public offers and commitments; the speech alone does not prove all promised work was completed.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3.

brief.significance: A self-funded adventuring and mutual-aid cooperative whose members lend equipment, organize craftspeople and supplies, welcome newcomers, and support public works and reconstruction.

actions.title: The Ale-Chemy Knights explain their mature economic system
actions.event: The Ale-Chemy Knights explain their mature economic system

brief.status: Key members repeatedly absent or missing
brief.basis: Existing public dossier, explicit status facts and named timeline participants. Selected events are a reading guide, not a complete list or a ranking of importance.

relationshipMap.title: Ale-Chemy Knights interaction map
relationshipMap.intro: Select a person, institution, or resource to trace their role, what they contribute, what the faction provides in return, and the limits of the recovered record. This is a historical network, not a current attendance roster.

nodes.title: Farkur
nodes.subtitle: Founder · organizer
nodes.history: Farkur and Ryvyt are identified as founders. Farkur directs specialist crafting to Ryvyt and records equipment loans.
nodes.consequence: Organizes pooled equipment, work, property, and newcomer support.
nodes.resource: Building expertise, organization, shared inventory and project coordination.
nodes.receives: The cooperative turns his plans into shared assets and a wider working network.
nodes.evidence: Tobias is a main member, not a proven founder. Farkur’s later disappearance has no established cause or outcome.
nodes.source: Knights record: main members; shop and inventory; missing Knights.

nodes.title: Ryvyt
nodes.subtitle: Founder · specialist crafter
nodes.history: In July 2025, Farkur marks Ryvyt’s requested equipment as loaned. In May 2026, Ryvyt calls himself the remaining founder.
nodes.consequence: Handles crafting beyond Farkur’s expertise and asks for project requests to be left for completion.
nodes.resource: Specialist crafting, research, and borrowed mission equipment.
nodes.receives: Borrows shared equipment for jobs, including the Hazewind Cape, Puzzler’s Wit ring, and a Bag of Holding.
nodes.evidence: That phrase does not establish Farkur’s death. Ryvyt’s personal research is not automatically faction policy.

nodes.title: Tobias
nodes.subtitle: Main member · builder & guide
nodes.history: Tobias turns the proposed newcomer service into witnessed support, helping adventurers become more independent.
nodes.consequence: Provides Fredrick with safety, food, a map, lodging and employment guidance, escort, and help with money.
nodes.resource: Building work, local orientation, escort, and personal financial assistance.
nodes.receives: The Knights’ welcome system supplies an institutional setting for his practical assistance.
nodes.evidence: Tobias is missing again by 8 Dec 2025; the earlier absence and later outcome remain unknown.
nodes.source: Knights record: welcome system; main members; December 2025.

nodes.title: Ruben
nodes.subtitle: Scout · operational representative
nodes.history: Ruben’s “Flight now, haul later” separates finding a resource from extracting and processing it.
nodes.consequence: Locates resources and explains how materials, paid labor, crafting, equipment, ships, and pooled money connect.
nodes.resource: Prospecting, maps, resource markings, and knowledge of the economic system.
nodes.receives: The wider organization can use preserved routes and transform discovered materials through its labor and supply network.
nodes.evidence: His operational role is established; complete rank and formal membership rules are not.
nodes.source: Knights record: late-2025 resources; 8 Dec 2025 economic system.

nodes.title: St. Anky
nodes.subtitle: Associate · religious intermediary
nodes.history: Anky is an important associate whose religious role belongs beside the cooperative’s practical work.
nodes.consequence: Appears in the Knights’ inner network and is known as their Saint.
nodes.resource: Religious mediation and close ties to the founder circle.
nodes.receives: Receives a place in the organization’s social and religious network; specific reciprocal material support is not recovered.
nodes.evidence: Exact formal membership or founder status is imprecise. The title Saint does not establish command authority.

nodes.title: Pristinia & Eovar
nodes.subtitle: Public works · property & transport
nodes.history: The collective votes to buy an Eovar tavern. Melian calls the Knights’ contributions invaluable; Severina connects their Eovar tower and wall works to public needs.
nodes.consequence: Public projects and customers give the cooperative work and places to invest its resources.
nodes.resource: Walls, towers, quarry work, tavern property, ships, and community labor.
nodes.receives: The Knights fund Pristinia fortifications, pay supervised newcomers, and supply infrastructure used in civic planning.
nodes.evidence: The full legal ownership of pooled assets and the durability of civic financial dependence remain unresolved.
nodes.source: Knights record: July property; public works; Apr–May 2026 civic power.

nodes.title: Gael market
nodes.subtitle: Reconstruction · skilled trade
nodes.history: By 19 Sep 2026, the market exists; Marius contrasts it with the region’s earlier lack of economy.
nodes.consequence: Gael provides the setting in which the Knights’ reconstruction model becomes a working civic institution.
nodes.resource: An open-air market divided by skill set.
nodes.receives: The Knights establish a specialized market where an economy can develop around skilled work.
nodes.evidence: Marius’s comparison remains attributed. The market’s complete staffing and management are not recovered.
nodes.source: Knights record: Gael reconstruction; regional history, 19 Sep 2026.

nodes.title: Gregory Greenleaf
nodes.subtitle: Financing critic · accountability
nodes.history: Ruben describes roughly ten percent of cost per mission, with ownership after a twelfth mission. Gregory challenges that arrangement.
nodes.consequence: Questions the effective cost of equipment financing and keeps the Knights’ claims of fairness open to challenge.
nodes.resource: Public ethical scrutiny of rental and financing terms.
nodes.receives: Receives an explanation of the proposed rental-to-ownership model; the record does not establish agreement.
nodes.evidence: Neither interpretation is an objective verdict. Gregory’s criticism is not evidence of membership or a permanent feud.

nodes.title: The Veilguard
nodes.subtitle: Separate faction · operational overlap
nodes.history: The two factions are explicitly separate even when people and operations overlap.
nodes.consequence: Offers a distinct protective network whose operations sometimes intersect with the Knights’ logistics.
nodes.resource: A protective company with shared recovery needs and inter-island ambitions.
nodes.receives: The Knights’ wider resources and contacts overlap with Veilguard operations; Ryvyt is a later operational link.
nodes.evidence: No merger, joint command, blanket alliance, or complete shared roster is established.
nodes.source: Veilguard record: people; open record; canon ruling, 3 Oct 2026.

insights.note: Only Farkur and Ryvyt are established founders.

insights.label: Working system
insights.note: Specialized labor and pooled assets connect practical needs.

insights.note: A confirmed reconstruction outcome by September 2026.
